---
title: "Prophet Model Implementation for Digital Payment Volume Forecasting with Holiday and Event Effects"
subtitle: "ATSA Group 2: Rohan Dedhia, Duncan D'lima, Sanaz Katpitia"
toc: false
---

We forecast daily UPI transaction volume with Prophet and test how much holidays and events improve the forecast.

::: {.callout-note}
NPCI publishes UPI data monthly only. The daily series here is **synthetic**, built from real NPCI monthly totals (Jan 2022 to Aug 2026) with holiday and event effects of known size. The results evaluate the modelling approach under these simulation assumptions; they are not validated real-world UPI forecast accuracy.
:::

## Key results

Out-of-sample errors from 10 rolling-origin folds with a 90-day horizon.

| Model | MAPE | WAPE | MAPE, 7-day horizon |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Seasonal naive | 5.54% | 5.56% | 4.43% |
| M2 SARIMAX | 4.97% | 5.05% | 3.01% |
| M3 Prophet base | 3.32% | 3.33% | 3.36% |
| M4 Prophet + holidays | 3.17% | 3.18% | 2.90% |
| **M5 Prophet + holidays + events** | **2.45%** | **2.44%** | **2.15%** |

- Adding holidays cut holiday-window error by about 30% (5.21% to 3.63%).
- Adding events halved sale-day error (8.57% to 4.33%).
- SARIMAX is competitive at short horizons but its error grows fastest with the horizon.
- Prophet recovers the payday effect almost exactly: 6.2% estimated against 6.0% true.
